Exp 9 — Edit attribution: attribute the update, undo its harmful part

Rank neurons by the causal push of their mask edit (all positions), inspect them on two corpora, then revert the top-k edits and measure the gap.

Setup
Task. Binary sentiment classification of movie reviews (IMDB-derived). The base LLM is frozen; a linear CLS head reads the final-token hidden state and predicts positive / negative.
Spurious setups (two regimes). bad (amplify): the ordinary word "bad" is made to correlate with the negative label. zxq (construct): a non-semantic token "zxq" is injected and made perfectly correlated with the negative label in training.
Models. Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
Masks. Sparse per-neuron MLP masks (hard-concrete L0) are trained on the frozen base + CLS head to solve the task. All interpretation and ablation here run with these learned masks turned ON — we analyze/remove neurons on top of the mask, not instead of it.
Evaluation. Balanced 2×2 validation set (label × cue-present), 2000 rows. gap = majority-group accuracy − minority-group accuracy, where the minority groups are pos+cue and neg+no-cue. A large gap means the model is leaning on the spurious cue.
This experiment (edit attribution + revert). Instead of ranking neurons by mask-edit size (uncorrelated with importance, ρ≈0.03–0.06) or by decision-token attribution (blind to cue-position detectors acting through attention), we attribute the update itself: the mask changed each neuron's contribution by (M−1)·h at every position, and Ej = Σpositions E[(M−1)·h·g] is grad×act applied to that change (ŷ = logitneg−logitpos, positive-label examples, masks on). E>0 = this edit pushes the shortcut; unedited neurons get exactly 0. We then revert (δ→0, i.e. M→1 exactly) the top-k edits and measure the gap — attributing the update and undoing its harmful part, one principle end-to-end. Each top neuron is interpreted on both corpora.
Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct  |  cue=bad
Edit attribution. Ej = Σpositions E[(Mj−1)·hj·gj] — grad×act applied to the mask-induced activation change, summed over all token positions (800 positive-label examples, masks on). 7535 neurons have shortcut-pushing edits (E>0); the top-30 hold 14% of the positive-E mass. Baseline gap +0.440; best intervention: revert all positiveE → gap +0.016 (Δ-0.424), overall 0.510 (Δ-0.251).
